newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Oil to charter double-hulled VLCC.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Oil to charter double-hulled VLCC.

text.p: Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd said on Thursday it will charter a double-hulled very large crude carrier (VLCC) from tanker operator Navix Line Ltd starting in 1999.
The 259,999 deadweight tonne ship, to be built by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd, will be the first double-hulled VLCC that Mitsubishi Oil has ever chartered, a company spokesman said.
The oil firm charters nine VLCCs on a long-term basis, and the eight other vessels in its fleet will also be replaced by double-hulled ones gradually, he added.

International Maritime Organisation (IMO) regulations now require all newly built tankers larger than 5,000 deadweight tonnes to be double-hulled or similarly reinforced to reduce the chance of an accidental oil spill.
The Russian tanker which broke into two in the Sea of Japan on January 2 and caused one of the worst oil spills to hit Japan was a single-hulled vessel, government officials said.
